rules: Project context: AuraRoll is a Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) app targeting both Android and iOS, with shared business logic in the `:shared` module (commonMain). Always think KMP-first when designing architecture: place data models, repositories, use cases, domain logic, and pure utilities in `shared/src/commonMain` so both platforms consume the same code. Only put platform-specific integrations under `androidMain`/`iosMain` (or in Android-only `feature/*` modules for Compose UI). Avoid leaking Android-only types (e.g. `android.graphics.Color`, `Context`, `Resources`, `Uri`, `Bitmap`, AndroidX/Compose types, `runBlocking` JVM-only behavior) into commonMain; use `expect`/`actual`, kotlinx primitives (`kotlinx.datetime`, `kotlinx.coroutines`, `kotlinx.serialization`, `kotlinx.collections.immutable`), or pure Kotlin equivalents. Repositories and use cases referenced by feature ViewModels must live in `:shared` whenever the same logic could run on iOS.

MVI one-off effect handling: Use the MVI pattern with State, Action, and Effect. Effects represent one-time side effects (toast, navigation, clipboard, intents, etc.) that must NOT be re-triggered on configuration change or recomposition.

Effect must live inside the UiState: Declare an `effect: <FeatureEffect>? = null` field inside a `UiState` (or equivalent) data class held within the feature's main immutable state (e.g. `AiChatState.ui.effect`). Do NOT expose effects via a separate Channel or SharedFlow.

Expose effect as a derived Flow from the state StateFlow: In the ViewModel, expose `val effect: Flow<FeatureEffect?> = state.map { it.ui.effect }`. Never collect the raw state to consume effects in the UI; only consume via the dedicated derived `effect` flow.

Mutate effect via `_uiState.update { it.copy(effect = ...) }`: All effect emissions must go through the same MutableStateFlow that owns the rest of UI state, so the snapshot is consistent and survives recombination in `combine { }` blocks.

Always provide a ConsumeEffect Action: Add an `Action.ConsumeEffect` that calls `_uiState.update { it.copy(effect = null) }`. The ViewModel must NEVER auto-clear the effect; clearing is driven by the UI after the side effect runs.

Activity/Composable consumes effects with the shared `LaunchedEffectHandler` Composable (located at `core/ui/src/main/java/com/what3words/core/ui/LaunchedEffectHandler.kt`). Pass `effectFlow = viewModel.effect`, implement side effects in `onEffect`, and dispatch `Action.ConsumeEffect` in `onConsumeEffect`. Do not write a custom `LaunchedEffect(effect) { ... }` for this purpose.

Effect handling lives in the Activity layer (or top-level screen Composable that has access to `LocalActivity`/launchers), not inside reusable child Composables. Pass `onAction: (Action) -> Unit` down; keep `LaunchedEffectHandler` colocated with platform integrations (Intents, Toasts, ActivityResultLaunchers, ClipboardManager, FileProvider, etc.).
Effects must be sealed types (`sealed interface FeatureEffect` or `sealed class`) with exhaustive `when` handling in the Activity. Do not use Strings, Ints, or Boolean flags as effects.
Never expose `LiveData<Event<T>>`, `Channel`, or `SharedFlow<Effect>` for one-off events in new code. The single-source-of-truth is the `UiState` and the derived effect Flow.

Unidirectional data flow: UI emits `Action`s via `viewModel.onAction(...)`; ViewModel updates `_uiState`; UI re-renders from `state`/derived flows. Effects follow the same loop (state -> derived flow -> UI consumes -> dispatches ConsumeEffect Action -> state cleared).

Static content / catalogue data (tips, quotes, copy banks, onboarding strings, hue keyword tables, etc.) MUST NOT be hardcoded inside Compose UI files (no top-level `private val FooList = listOf(...)` next to a Composable, no inline lists in `@Preview`-adjacent code). Model it as a domain entity in `shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/helios/auraroll/<feature>/` following the `HueQuote` / `HueQuoteRepository` / `DefaultHueQuoteRepository` pattern: 1) a pure-Kotlin data class for the item, 2) a repository interface exposing the catalogue, 3) a `Default<Name>Repository` impl owning the static list, 4) a Hilt `@Provides` binding in the feature's `RepositoryProviderModule`, 5) inject the repository into the ViewModel and surface the data via `UiState`. The Composable consumes `uiState.<field>` only and must remain free of business/content data. This keeps copy reusable on iOS, swappable for remote-driven sources, and testable without Compose.
